rationale: The sign conventions on recch/invch are handled correctly and the ZSCORE-centering does isolate a slope-steepening interaction rather than a leverage tilt, but the construct is still fundamentally the Sloan accrual anomaly re-weighted by a distress proxy — a well-trodden conditioning that will need a large incremental t-stat over plain accruals to justify itself.

target_name: Supplier Credit Stretching In Deficit Firms
rationale: The sign-reversal hypothesis for payables in deficit firms is genuinely interesting, but the stated claim that "a negative slope can only come from the interaction" is false — the product of two uncentered [0,1] ranks loads heavily on both main effects, so the signal will largely reproduce the known low-retained-earnings/distress return effect unless at least one leg is demeaned.

target_name: Working Capital Accruals Only In Loss Firms
rationale: Masking the accrual measure to zero for the profitable majority creates a point mass covering most of the cross-section, which will make quantile sorts degenerate and the FF5 spread a thin loss-firm-only bet, and the underlying claim (accrual mispricing concentrated in loss/distressed firms) is already documented rather than novel.

A non-current-accrual manipulation channel is a legitimately different test from the working-capital variants and the centering is done properly, but DELTA(dp/sale) is dominated by movements in the sales denominator, so the signal risks being a repackaged sales-growth/asset-growth effect that happens to point the same direction — a fact the proposal never acknowledges.

The economic reading is ambiguous — a rising taxes-payable balance most commonly reflects higher current profitability, not involuntary deferral — and the construct compounds this with sparse/lumpy txp coverage and an uncentered rank product that again loads on the standalone distress main effect the authors claim to have neutralized.

Receivable and inventory growth measured against contracting sales is essentially the Abarbanell-Bushee fundamental signals (inventory and receivables growth relative to sales growth) and the Thomas-Zhang inventory-change anomaly, so this is a direct rediscovery, further weakened by an uncentered rank product that mixes in the standalone accrual and sales-growth effects.
